In this series we build a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) from scratch, covering
every building block from the ground up. The tutorial is split into five parts
that progressively assemble the full generative pipeline.

## Table of Contents

1. [**Transformer Architecture**](../transformer/transformer.qmd) — Multi-head
   self-attention, feed-forward blocks, layer normalization, and residual
   connections. The foundation that everything else builds on.

2. [**Autoencoder Architecture**](../autoencoder/autoencoder.qmd) — Convolutional encoder and decoder that
   compress pixel-space images into a compact latent representation and
   reconstruct them back. This separates "what the image looks like" from
   "how to generate it".

3. [**Class-Conditional VAE**](../class_conditional_vae/class_conditional_vae.qmd) —
   Conditioning a VAE on class labels so the decoder knows *what* to generate
   while the latent code encodes *how*. Implements spatial concatenation and
   adaLN conditioning — the same mechanism used by DiT.

4. [**The Diffusion Paradigm**](../the_diffusion_paradigm/the_diffusion_paradigm.qmd) — Forward noising process, noise schedules
   (linear and cosine), the reparameterization trick, and DDPM reverse
   sampling. How we turn the generation problem into a denoising problem.

5. **ViT: Vision Transformer** — Patch embedding, positional encoding, and
   the full Vision Transformer. Adapting the transformer architecture to
   operate on images by treating them as sequences of patches.

6. **DiT: Diffusion Transformer** *(current entry)* — Adaptive Layer Norm
   (adaLN), timestep and label conditioning, DiT blocks, and the complete
   latent-space denoising network. Putting it all together to generate
   FashionMNIST images.
